title: Power Round — Spring 2025 — ARML Power sub-problem rubric

criteria.name: Problem 1
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1 (3 pts). Statement: 1.

criteria.name: Problem 2
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 2 (3 pts). Statement: 2. Show, by writing out all possible cases, that B(50) = 5 and that there is only one Fibonacci-like sequence with b = 5 that contains the number 50.

criteria.name: Problem 3
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 3 (2 pts). Statement: 3. Showing work, compute B(22).

criteria.name: Problem 4
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 4 (3 pts). Statement: 4. Note that the general Fibonacci-like sequence F (a, b) begins a, b, a + b, a + 2b, 2a + 3b, 3a + 5b, 5a + 8b, . . . . You might recognize those coeﬃcients of a and b as the regular Fibonacci numbers. Prove that for k ≥ 3 that F (a, b)k = Fk−2a + Fk−1b. (This relationship actually holds for all integers k, by running the sequences backward as explained in the background material.)

criteria.name: Problem 5
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 5 (2 pts). Statement: 5. Prove that if F (a1, b)k = F (a2, b)k then a1 = a2. That is, if the same number occurs in the same location in two Fibonacci-like sequences with the same b value, they must be the exact same sequence.

criteria.name: Problem 6
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 6 (2 pts). Statement: 6. Prove that for any integers 1 ≤ j < k that Fk− Fk−j Fk−j−1 ≥ 1, with equality if and only if j = 1.

criteria.name: Problem 7
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 7 (4 pts). Statement: 7. Let F (a, b)k = F (a′, b′)k−j for some 1 ≤ j < k . That is, the same number appears in both Fibonacci-like sequences F (a, b) and F (a′, b′) but appears earlier in the latter. Prove that b < b′.

criteria.name: Problem 8
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 8 (2 pts). Statement: 8. Given a Fibonacci-like sequence a1, a2, a3, . . . , ak−1, ak that contains ak = n. Let b1, b2, . . . , bk be another sequence of the same length, with bk = ak = n that also satis- ﬁes the Fibonacci recursion, and that bk−1 = ak−1−1. Show that bk−j = ak−j+(−1)jFj.

criteria.name: Problem 9a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 9a (1 pt). Statement: 9. Lengthen each Fibonacci-like sequence backward as far as possible while staying Fibonacci- like: (a) 11 , 17, . . ..

criteria.name: Problem 9b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 9b (1 pt). Statement: (b) 6 , 8, . . ..

criteria.name: Problem 9c
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 9c (1 pt). Statement: (c) 7 , 16, . . ..

criteria.name: Problem 10a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 10a (2 pts). Statement: 10. Given a≤ b, under what conditions on a and b may the sequence a, b, . . . be extended backward (a) by exactly one term?

criteria.name: Problem 10b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 10b (2 pts). Statement: (b) by two or more terms?

criteria.name: Problem 11
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 11 (3 pts). Statement: 11. Use this algorithm to ﬁnd B(199) and B(201).

criteria.name: Problem 12
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 12 (4 pts). Statement: 12. Prove that algorithm is correct. That is, given any positive integer n, prove the al- gorithm always stops after a ﬁnite number of steps and produces the correct value of B(n).

criteria.name: Problem 13
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 13 (2 pts). Statement: 13. Prove that if each sequence is lengthened as much as possible, then for each positive integer b there are exactly 1 + ⌊(b− 1)/2⌋ Fibonacci-like sequences with b as their second term.

criteria.name: Problem 14
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 14 (3 pts). Statement: 14. For each b in the range 1 ≤ b≤ 10, compute L(b), which is the least number n such that B(n) = b. (Note: if you ﬁnd that one of these values is larger than 100 you have made an error.)
